neighbours.label: the comma that closes a fronted subordinate clause (since / while / when / if ... ,) before the main clause
fire: Because the bridge was closed for repairs, we drove the long way.
While the oven heats up, chop the onions and garlic.
Since the shop opens at nine, there is no need to hurry.
When the rain finally stopped, the children went outside.
Although the film was long, nobody left the cinema early.
As soon as the bell rang, the students packed their bags.
Unless the train is late, we will arrive before dinner.
After the guests had gone home, she washed the dishes.
quiet: We drove the long way because the bridge was closed for repairs.
Chop the onions and garlic while the oven heats up.
There is no need to hurry since the shop opens at nine.
The children went outside when the rain finally stopped.
Nobody left the cinema early although the film was long.
The students packed their bags as soon as the bell rang.
We will arrive before dinner unless the train is late.
She washed the dishes after the guests had gone home.

notes: near misses put the same clause after the main clause, so there is no clause-closing comma.
